items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: Now the first drummer when we came back, we hired a boy named Wilbur Kirk. ... He played with us that whole season.

ctx.x: A few years before that. And, one thing we did started from our opening night, if we got a request for a piece if -- we knew it we'd play it and we kept a file of different tunes and -- that different friends would come in and like. And once we knew a person and knew the song they liked, they would never have to ask for that song anymore, because when they'd walk down the steps coming into that club, we would start playing their favorite song. Now this is what helped put the band over.

And, we thought of it as being a nice public relations sort of thing, to please the patrons and keep them coming to the nightclub. So the band opened and the band was a riot. Saturday nights you couldn't get them in there. They were always having to turn away 50 or 100 people. The floor shows were a hit, out of this world. Now the first drummer when we came back, we hired a boy named Wilbur Kirk. Wilbur Kirk was a very fine drummer, he knew the fundamentals of the drums.
He played with us that whole season. Noble Sissle came through town and Wilbur Kirk joined Noble Sissle and so did our guitarist.
